hints: Write a general point on the line as $(1+\lambda,3-2\lambda,-2+3\lambda)$.
Substitute these coordinates into $2x+y-3z=5$ and solve for $\lambda$.
Put that parameter back into the line equation and report the resulting position vector.
walkthrough:
Express the coordinates of a general point on line $l$ in terms of parameter $\lambda$:
$$x = 1 + \lambda, \quad y = 3 - 2\lambda, \quad z = -2 + 3\lambda$$

Substitute these coordinates into the equation of plane $p$: $2x + y - 3z = 5$:
$$2(1 + \lambda) + (3 - 2\lambda) - 3(-2 + 3\lambda) = 5$$

Substitute $\lambda = \dfrac{2}{3}$ into the coordinates of line $l$:
- $x = 1 + \dfrac{2}{3} = \dfrac{5}{3}$
- $y = 3 - 2\left(\dfrac{2}{3}\right) = \dfrac{5}{3}$
- $z = -2 + 3\left(\dfrac{2}{3}\right) = 0$

State the position vector of the point of intersection:
$$\mathbf{r} = \dfrac{5}{3}\mathbf{i} + \dfrac{5}{3}\mathbf{j} \quad \left(\text{or } \begin{pmatrix} 5/3 \\ 5/3 \\ 0 \end{pmatrix}\right)$$

hints: The angle between a line and a plane is complementary to the angle between the line direction and the plane normal.
Apply $\sin\theta=|\mathbf d\cdot\mathbf n|/(|\mathbf d||\mathbf n|)$ directly for the acute line-plane angle, then evaluate it.
walkthrough:
Identify the direction vector $\mathbf{d}$ of line $l$ and the normal vector $\mathbf{n}$ to plane $p$:
$$\mathbf{d} = \begin{pmatrix} 1 \\ -2 \\ 3 \end{pmatrix}, \quad \mathbf{n} = \begin{pmatrix} 2 \\ 1 \\ -3 \end{pmatrix}$$

Recall the formula for the acute angle $\theta$ between a line and a plane:
$$\sin\theta = \dfrac{|\mathbf{d} \cdot \mathbf{n}|}{|\mathbf{d}||\mathbf{n}|}$$

Calculate the magnitudes of both vectors:
$$|\mathbf{d}| = \sqrt{1^2 + (-2)^2 + 3^2} = \sqrt{1 + 4 + 9} = \sqrt{14}$$
$$|\mathbf{n}| = \sqrt{2^2 + 1^2 + (-3)^2} = \sqrt{4 + 1 + 9} = \sqrt{14}$$
$$|\mathbf{d}||\mathbf{n}| = \sqrt{14} \times \sqrt{14} = 14$$

Round to 1 decimal place (or 3 significant figures):
$$\theta \approx 40.0^\circ \quad (\text{or } 0.698 \text{ radians})$$

hints: A plane containing $l$ has a normal perpendicular to the line direction; being perpendicular to $p$ also makes its normal perpendicular to the normal of $p$.
Find a normal to $q$ from $(1,-2,3)\times(2,1,-3)$, up to a non-zero scalar multiple.
Use the fixed point $(1,3,-2)$ from line $l$ in the Cartesian plane equation.
Determine the right-hand side by substitution and check that another point on $l$ also satisfies the equation.
walkthrough: Plane $q$ contains line $l$, so it is parallel to direction vector $\mathbf{d} = \begin{pmatrix} 1 \\ -2 \\ 3 \end{pmatrix}$. Plane $q$ is perpendicular to plane $p$, so its normal vector is perpendicular to $\mathbf{n}_p = \begin{pmatrix} 2 \\ 1 \\ -3 \end{pmatrix}$.

Find the normal vector $\mathbf{n}_q$ to plane $q$ using the cross product $\mathbf{d} \times \mathbf{n}_p$:
$$\mathbf{n}_q = \begin{vmatrix} \mathbf{i} & \mathbf{j} & \mathbf{k} \\ 1 & -2 & 3 \\ 2 & 1 & -3 \end{vmatrix}$$
$$= \mathbf{i}\bigl((-2)(-3) - (3)(1)\bigr) - \mathbf{j}\bigl((1)(-3) - (3)(2)\bigr) + \mathbf{k}\bigl((1)(1) - (-2)(2)\bigr)$$
$$= \mathbf{i}(6 - 3) - \mathbf{j}(-3 - 6) + \mathbf{k}(1 + 4)$$
$$= 3\mathbf{i} + 9\mathbf{j} + 5\mathbf{k} = \begin{pmatrix} 3 \\ 9 \\ 5 \end{pmatrix}$$

Write the equation of plane $q$ in Cartesian form:
$$3x + 9y + 5z = d$$

Substitute the coordinates of point $(1, 3, -2)$ on line $l$ to determine $d$:
$$d = 3(1) + 9(3) + 5(-2) = 3 + 27 - 10 = 20$$

Verify with the point of intersection $\left(\dfrac{5}{3}, \dfrac{5}{3}, 0\right)$:
$$3\left(\dfrac{5}{3}\right) + 9\left(\dfrac{5}{3}\right) + 5(0) = 5 + 15 + 0 = 20 \quad \text{(verified)}$$
